deep.reconstruction:
Context: the page sits in an interleaved arithmetic textbook (the facing printed page is on cube roots). Gauss's notes are about the dilogarithm, which he calls φ. Line 1 defines φx = ∫ dx/x · l(1/(1−x)) = −∫_0^x ln(1−t)/t dt = Li2(x). He first wrote l(...), struck it out, and wrote l(1/(1−x)) above.

(1) Integration by parts. ∫ dx/x · ln(1/(1−x)) = ln x · ln(1/(1−x)) − ∫ ln x · dx/(1−x). He first wrote x in the denominator, struck it out, and replaced it by 1−x. [My filling-in] Put t = 1−s in ∫_0^x ln t/(1−t) dt. This gives ∫_{1−x}^1 ln(1−s)/s ds = Li2(1−x) − Li2(1). That leads to Euler's reflection formula, Li2(x) + Li2(1−x) = π²/6 − ln x · ln(1−x). Gauss writes 'φx + φ(1−x) = lx·l 1−x + ππ/6'. This is correct only if 'l 1−x' is read as l(1/(1−x)), as in line 1. Read literally as ln(1−x), the sign of the log product is wrong.

(2) Inversion. Substitute x = 1/y. Then dx/x = −dy/y and ln(1−1/y) = ln(1−y) − ln y + const. He writes ∫ dx/x · l(1−x) = ∫ dy/y · l y − ∫ dy/y · l(1−y), suppressing the constant iπ / branch term. From this he states φx + φ(1/x) = (lx)²/2 + π²/3; a struck symbol follows. The correct formula is Li2(x) + Li2(1/x) = −π²/6 − ½ ln²(−x). For real x > 1 the real part is π²/3 − ½ ln² x. The constant π²/3 fits φ = Li2 (check x = 1: 2ζ(2) = π²/3). The +½ ln² x would fit the other convention, φ = ∫ dx/x · ln(1−x) = −Li2. So conventions are mixed and there is a sign slip.

(3) Gauss records 1 − 1/4 + 1/9 − 1/16 + ... = π²/12. This is −Li2(−1) = η(2), and it is correct.

(4) Evaluating φ(√−1) + φ(−√−1). Since 1/i = −i, his inversion formula with x = i gives (ln i)²/2 + π²/3 = −π²/8 + π²/3 = 5π²/24. This is what he writes; the 24 is overwritten. A line below, apparently another attempt with denominator 12, is heavily struck out. The true value is Li2(i) + Li2(−i) = ½ Li2(−1) = −π²/24. This also equals −π²/6 − ½(ln(−i))² = −π²/6 + π²/8.

(5) He then separates the series Li2(i) = Σ iⁿ/n² = i − 1/4 − i/9 + 1/16 + i/25 − ... He numbers the terms 1…8 and writes out the imaginary part, 1 − 1/9 + 1/25 − 1/49 ... = (left blank; this is Catalan's constant G). He also writes the real part, (1/4 − 1/16 + 1/36 ...) = ¼ · π²/12 = π²/48, with Re Li2(i) = −π²/48. This check gives Li2(i) + Li2(−i) = 2 Re Li2(i) = −π²/24, which exposes the error in (4); presumably this is why he struck out the second line. He leaves the value of G open, as it has no closed form.

The freehand curve with a crossing line at left is an unexplained sketch, apparently unrelated.
errors: φx+φ(1−x) = lx·l(1−x) + π²/6: if 'l 1−x' means ln(1−x), the sign of the product is wrong. The correct form is π²/6 − ln x ln(1−x) = π²/6 + ln x · ln(1/(1−x)).

φx+φ(1/x) = (lx)²/2 + π²/3: the sign of the log-square term is wrong for φ = Li2. The real-part form for x > 1 is π²/3 − (ln x)²/2; generally it is −π²/6 − ½ ln²(−x). The constant follows one sign convention for φ and the log term the other.
The inversion integral identity drops the constant ln(−1) = iπ (a branch term) without comment.

φ(i)+φ(−i) = 5π²/24 is wrong; the correct value is −π²/24. It follows from inserting x = i into the sign-erroneous inversion formula. The struck line and the real/imaginary decomposition below suggest Gauss noticed this.

results.what: Integration by parts of ∫ ln(1/(1−x)) dx/x and reflection formula Li2(x)+Li2(1−x) = π²/6 − ln x ln(1−x)
results.modern_name: Euler's reflection formula for the dilogarithm

results.what: Inversion relation Li2(x)+Li2(1/x) = π²/3 − ½ln²x (real part, x>1)
Attempt at Li2(i)+Li2(−i), and splitting Li2(i) into the real part −π²/48 and the imaginary part 1 − 1/9 + 1/25 − ... (Catalan's constant)
results.usually_credited_to: Euler / Landen for the duplication relation; the constant G is named after Catalan (1865), though the series was treated earlier (Euler, Bernoulli)

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard 18th-century dilogarithm identities (Euler, Landen), worked out here with sign slips. Gauss's familiarity with such series is expected from his work on the hypergeometric series. Nothing goes beyond known results; the attempt at Li2(i) contains an error.

checkable.asserts: Reflection: the derivative of Li2(x)+Li2(1−x)+ln x ln(1−x) is 0, so the sum is constant.
Real-part inversion for x > 1 has −½ln²x, not +½ln²x (result ≈ 0).
Im Li2(i) = Catalan's G = 1 − 1/9 + 1/25 − ...; Re Li2(i) = −π²/48.
Gauss's 5π²/24 comes from plugging x = i into his (sign-flawed) inversion formula (result ≈ 0).

transcription_corrections: Line 1: the integrand l(...) is struck out and replaced by l(1/(1−x)), written above. The right side is lx · l(1/(1−x)).
Line 2: the denominator x is struck out and replaced by 1−x: −∫ dx/(1−x) · lx.
The symbol after +ππ/6 and after +ππ/3 is a struck-through mark, not part of the formula.
φ√−1 + φ(−√−1) = 5ππ/24: the denominator is overwritten as 24, and the line below (denominator 12) is heavily struck.
Bottom row: the numbers 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 index the terms of Σ iⁿ/n². The row '1/2? 1/4 − 1/16 + 1/36' lists the real-part terms (the first symbol may be a stray mark or 1/2).
